Distinct from `VetoOpponentNonHandCasts` (Drannith Magistrate), which is opponents-only and sweeps in EVERY non-hand zone including exile — the two mechanisms are independent and compose. **[dur: continuous — active for self's battlefield lifetime]**
backend/scripts/skills/primitive-catalog.md:1126:- `cardfns.CountPlayersAttackedThisCombat(gs) int` (cardfns/lib_count_players_attacked.go) — walks the battlefield for every `Attacking` creature and resolves the DEFENDING player per-attacker: `Card.AttackTarget.Controller` when attacking a planeswalker (Rule 506.4c/508.1d, set by `DeclareAttackersWithTargets`), otherwise `1 - Controller` (direct player attack), then dedupes into a distinct-player count. No new engine state — reads existing `Attacking`/`AttackTarget`/`Controller` fields live, so it's always current mid-combat (redeclaring or removing an attacker changes the result on the very next call). Battles aren't modeled by this engine yet (no `Card.IsBattle`/protector concept exists), so they're out of scope; add a case if that lands. Note: the live `DeclareAttackers`/`DeclareAttackersWithTargets` pipeline is itself 2-player-shaped (every direct attack in one combat call targets the same hard-coded `1 - playerIdx` opponent) — the planeswalker path is what lets the count exceed 1 on a genuinely multiplayer battlefield, since `AttackTarget` can point at a planeswalker belonging to any seat. **[dur: one-shot — recomputed fresh on every call, nothing persists]**

// patternTargetPlayerDrawsCards matches the simple "Target player draws N cards." form.
// Example: Can't Quite Recall (MB2)
func patternTargetPlayerDrawsCards() *Pattern {
	return &Pattern{
		ID:          "target_player_draws_cards",
		Name:        "Target Player Draws Cards",
		Description: "Target player draws N cards",
		Examples:    []string{"Can't Quite Recall"},
		Regex:       regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^Target player draws (\w+|\d+) cards?\.?$`),
		CardTypes:   []string{"Instant", "Sorcery"},
		Priority:    50,
		Template: func(matches []string, cardType string) []AbilityDSL {
			amount := parseWordNumber(matches[1])
			return []AbilityDSL{
				{
					Type:   "spell",
					Effect: "draw",
					Value:  map[string]interface{}{"amount": amount},

// patternTargetPlayerDrawsCardsAndLosesLife matches "Target player draws N cards and loses N life."

func patternTargetPlayerDrawsCardsAndLosesLife() *Pattern {
	return &Pattern{
		ID:          "target_player_draws_cards_and_loses_life",
		Name:        "Target Player Draws Cards and Loses Life",
		Description: "Target player draws N cards and loses N life",
		Examples:    []string{"Toil"},
		Regex:       regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^Target player draws (\w+|\d+) cards? and loses (\d+|\w+) life\.?$`),
		CardTypes:   []string{"Instant", "Sorcery"},
		Priority:    44,
		Template: func(matches []string, cardType string) []AbilityDSL {
			drawAmount := parseWordNumber(matches[1])

// AbilityDSL represents a parsed ability in DSL format
type AbilityDSL struct {
	Type    string                 `json:"type"`              // static, triggered, activated, spell
	Effect  string                 `json:"effect"`            // pump, grant, damage, draw, destroy, etc.
	Value   map[string]interface{} `json:"value,omitempty"`   // {power: 1, toughness: 1}
	Keyword string                 `json:"keyword,omitempty"` // for grant effects
	Trigger string                 `json:"trigger,omitempty"` // etb, dies, attacks, upkeep
	Cost    *AbilityCost           `json:"cost,omitempty"`    // for activated abilities
	Affects *TargetFilter          `json:"affects,omitempty"` // who is affected
	Target  *TargetFilter          `json:"target,omitempty"`  // targeting requirements

	// ---- Paragraph Schema v2 (docs/paragraph-schema-v2.md, adapter step 3a) ----
	// All optional; absent on every v1 record. Use DerivedTrigger()/
	// DerivedEffects() to read the v2 view regardless of record generation.
	TriggerV2 *TriggerSpec `json:"trigger_v2,omitempty"` // factored trigger object (Change 1)
	Effects   []EffectAtom `json:"effects,omitempty"`    // ordered effect sequence (Change 3)
	Condition *Condition   `json:"condition,omitempty"`  // "as long as ..." for statics (Change 2)
}

// AbilityCost represents the cost of an activated ability
type AbilityCost struct {
	Tap            bool          `json:"tap,omitempty"`

	Mana           game.ManaCost `json:"mana,omitempty"`
	Sacrifice      string        `json:"sacrifice,omitempty"`       // "creature", "permanent", "self", etc.
	SacrificeCount int           `json:"sacrifice_count,omitempty"` // number to sacrifice (default 1, e.g. "Sacrifice two Blood tokens")
	Life           int           `json:"life,omitempty"`
	Energy         int           `json:"energy,omitempty"`       // Pay N {E} (Rule 106.11)
	DiscardSelf    bool          `json:"discard_self,omitempty"` // Discard this card (Channel etc.)
	DiscardN       int           `json:"discard_n,omitempty"`    // Discard N cards as cost
	DiscardHand    bool          `json:"discard_hand,omitempty"` // Discard your hand as cost (e.g. Lion's Eye Diamond)
	MillN          int           `json:"mill_n,omitempty"`       // Mill N cards from your own library as cost (e.g. "Mill a card:", "Mill two cards:")
	Additional     string        `json:"additional,omitempty"`   // "tap_another_creature", "discard", etc.
	Restriction    string        `json:"restriction,omitempty"`  // "metalcraft", "threshold:3:artifact", etc.

	// TapOther: "Tap another/an untapped X you control" — a SINGLE permanent,
	// chosen by the activating player (a real choice — see
	// game.ActivationCost.TapOther), as opposed to TapOthers below which
	// taps a fixed COUNT where which ones is not a meaningful choice.
	// Closed-vocabulary string, "_"-joined (matchSimpleTapType): base type
	// (creature/artifact/land/enchantment/planeswalker/permanent),
	// "legendary" qualifier, a color name, or a subtype — e.g.

	// of ReturnToHand below (which carries a TargetFilter+Count but is not
	// wired to game.ActivationCost at all — no declarative pathway exists

	// TapOther (game.ActivationCost.ReturnOther / matchesReturnOtherType,
	// which reuses matchSimpleTapType), just without the untapped
	// requirement — e.g. "artifact", "land", "legendary_creature".
	ReturnOther string `json:"return_other,omitempty"`

	// ---- Paragraph Schema v2 cost extensions (Change 6, adapter step 3a) ----
	RemoveCounters *CounterCost   `json:"remove_counters,omitempty"` // Remove N TYPE counters from X
	TapOthers      *TapOthersCost `json:"tap_others,omitempty"`      // Tap N untapped X you control
	ExileCost      *ExileCost     `json:"exile,omitempty"`           // Exile self/N cards from zone
	ReturnToHand   *ReturnCost    `json:"return_to_hand,omitempty"`  // Return X to owner's hand
	Tag            string         `json:"tag,omitempty"`             // exhaust|boast|forecast|... (closed)
	RestrictionV2  string         `json:"restriction_v2,omitempty"`  // V2CostRestrictions enum
	Condition      *Condition     `json:"cost_condition,omitempty"`  // "Activate only if ..."

	// CostReductionSpec — "This ability costs {N} less to activate for each
	// X" (task-1980 static_cost_mod). Same closed dynamic count-spec shape

	CostReductionSpec map[string]interface{} `json:"cost_reduction_spec,omitempty"`
}

// ToGameCard converts a CardDefinition to a game.Card
func (def *CardDefinition) ToGameCard(owner int) (*game.Card, error) {
	var cardType game.CardType
	switch def.Type {
	case "Land":
		cardType = game.TypeLand
	case "Creature":
		cardType = game.TypeCreature
	case "Instant":
		cardType = game.TypeInstant
	case "Sorcery":
		cardType = game.TypeSorcery
	case "Artifact":
		cardType = game.TypeArtifact
	case "Enchantment":
		cardType = game.TypeEnchantment
	case "Planeswalker":
		cardType = game.TypePlaneswalker
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown card type: %s", def.Type)
	}

	// Create the card based on type
	var card *game.Card
	if def.Type == "Land" {
		card = game.NewLand(def.Name, def.LandType, owner)
	} else if def.Type == "Creature" {
		power := 0
		toughness := 0
		if def.Power != nil {
			power = *def.Power
		}
		if def.Toughness != nil {
			toughness = *def.Toughness
		}
		card = game.NewCreature(def.Name, def.ManaCost, power, toughness, owner)
	} else if def.Type == "Instant" {
		// Check for spell effect in abilities
		spellEffect := def.GetSpellEffect()
		def.liftSecondaryTokenEffect(spellEffect)
		def.liftSecondaryLifeGainEffect(spellEffect)
		def.liftSecondaryEndTurnEffect(spellEffect)
		if spellEffect != nil {
			card = game.NewInstant(def.Name, def.ManaCost, spellEffect, owner)
		} else {
			card = game.NewCard(def.Name, cardType, def.ManaCost, owner)
		}
	} else if def.Type == "Sorcery" {
		// Check for spell effect in abilities
		spellEffect := def.GetSpellEffect()
		def.liftSecondaryTokenEffect(spellEffect)
		def.liftSecondaryLifeGainEffect(spellEffect)
		def.liftSecondaryEndTurnEffect(spellEffect)
		if spellEffect != nil {
			card = game.NewSorcery(def.Name, def.ManaCost, spellEffect, owner)
		} else {
			card = game.NewCard(def.Name, cardType, def.ManaCost, owner)
		}
	} else {
		card = game.NewCard(def.Name, cardType, def.ManaCost, owner)
	}

	card.SubTypes = def.SubTypes
	card.Types = append([]string(nil), def.Types...)
	card.Colors = def.Colors

	// printed keyword must set Card.ReboundData itself — gamestate.go's

	// other spell.
	if card.HasKeyword(game.Rebound) {

	card.Legendary = def.Legendary

	if def.Type == "Planeswalker" && def.StartingLoyalty > 0 {
		card.Counters.Loyalty = def.StartingLoyalty

	// REPARSE-MAP static_unmapped / "Creatures with power less than ~'s
	// power can't block it" family, e.g. Aura Gnarlid, Battering Wurm):
	// cardfns/DenProtector.go proves this restriction already works end to
	// end through cardfns.RestrictBlockersTo, but only as a bespoke
	// per-card CardHandler keyed by exact card name — precisely because no
	// registered primitive expressed the clause. This bridges the SAME
	// mechanism onto the DSL: a static ability atom naming this effect
	// registers an equivalent closure into game.CardHandlers for THIS
	// card's own name, so any carddb entry can carry the clause without a
	// hand-written CardHandler of its own.
	for _, ab := range def.Abilities {

			continue

				continue
			}

				if RestrictBlockersToFn == nil {

				}

// Package game implements Magic targeting according to Rule 114, 601.2c, 608.2b
package game

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

// TargetType defines what kind of target is required
type TargetType string

// CanBeTargetedBy checks if a card can be targeted by a spell/ability controlled by a player
// Rule 702.11: Hexproof - Can't be targeted by spells or abilities opponents control
// Rule 702.18: Shroud - Can't be targeted by any spells or abilities
func CanBeTargetedBy(card *Card, controllerIdx int, em *EffectManager) bool {
	// Rule 702.18: Shroud - can't be targeted by anyone, including its controller
	if card.HasKeywordWithEffects(Shroud, em) {
		return false
	}

	// Rule 702.11: Hexproof - can't be targeted by opponents
	if card.HasKeywordWithEffects(Hexproof, em) {
		// Hexproof only protects from opponents, owner can still target
		if card.Controller != controllerIdx {
			return false // Opponent can't target this
		}
	}

	return true
}

// CanBeTargetedByCard checks if a target card can be targeted by a source card
// Rule 702.16: Protection prevents targeting (the "T" in DEBT)
func CanBeTargetedByCard(target *Card, source *Card, em *EffectManager) bool {
	// First check shroud and hexproof
	if source == nil {
		return CanBeTargetedBy(target, -1, em)
	}

	if !CanBeTargetedBy(target, source.Controller, em) {
		return false
	}

	// Rule 702.16: Protection prevents targeting by sources with the protected quality
	if target.HasProtectionFromCard(source) {
		return false
	}

	// Rule 702.11c: color-scoped Hexproof (e.g. "Hexproof from blue") prevents
	// targeting by opponent-controlled sources matching that quality
	if target.HasHexproofFromCard(source) {
		return false
	}

	return true
}

func TestExecuteDrawEffect_TargetPlayer(t *testing.T) {
	gs := NewGame("P0", "P1", false)
	source := NewCreature("Test Draw Source", ManaCost{}, 1, 1, 0)
	source.Owner, source.Controller = 0, 0
	gs.Battlefield.AddCard(source)

	before0 := len(gs.Players[0].Hand.GetAll())
	before1 := len(gs.Players[1].Hand.GetAll())

	stackObj := &StackObject{
		IsAbility:   true,
		Text:        "draw",
		Controller:  0,
		Card:        source,
		EffectValue: map[string]interface{}{"amount": float64(2)},
		Targets:     []Target{{IsCard: false, PlayerIdx: 1}},
	}

	if err := gs.ExecuteAbilityEffect(stackObj); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ExecuteAbilityEffect: %v", err)
	}

	after0 := len(gs.Players[0].Hand.GetAll())
	after1 := len(gs.Players[1].Hand.GetAll())

	if after1-before1 != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("target player (idx 1) drew %d cards, want 2", after1-before1)
	}
	if after0 != before0 {
		t.Fatalf("controller (idx 0) hand changed by %d, want 0 (target player should draw instead)", after0-before0)
	}
}

// executeTargetPlayerDrawDiscard handles "{T}: Target player draws N cards,
// then discards M cards." (Reckless Scholar). The chosen player both draws and
// discards; the discard opens a PendingChoice for that same player. Falls back
// to the controller when no player target was supplied.
func (gs *GameState) executeTargetPlayerDrawDiscard(controller int, effectValue map[string]interface{}, targets []Target) error {
	drawN := getIntValue(effectValue, "draw", 1)
	discardN := getIntValue(effectValue, "discard", 1)

	targetPlayer := controller
	if len(targets) > 0 && !targets[0].IsCard {
		targetPlayer = targets[0].PlayerIdx
	}
	if targetPlayer < 0 || targetPlayer >= len(gs.Players) {
		return nil
	}

	if drawN > 0 {
		if err := gs.DrawCardsWithEvent(targetPlayer, drawN); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}

	if discardN <= 0 {
		return nil
	}

	player := gs.Players[targetPlayer]
	if player.Hand.Count() == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	count := discardN
	if player.Hand.Count() < count {
		count = player.Hand.Count()
	}

	candidates := make([]string, 0, player.Hand.Count())
	for _, c := range player.Hand.GetAll() {
		candidates = append(candidates, c.ID)
	}

	gs.PendingChoice = &PendingChoice{
		PlayerIdx:  targetPlayer,
		ChoiceType: "hand_discard",
		Candidates: candidates,
		Count:      count,
	}
	return nil
}

// spellControllerTargetType folds a SPELL sequence atom's controller-
// qualified creature Target ({Filter:"creature", Controller:"you"|
// "opponent"}, nothing else set) onto the matching composite TargetType —
// the same TargetCreatureYouCtl/TargetCreatureOppCtl enum "token_copy" and
// the struct-path "pump_until_eot" case already trust for spell-level cast
// legality. Returns "" for anything else (bare filter, a different
// controller value, or any additional qualifier), leaving the caller's
// existing bare/unsupported handling untouched (task-2449, verb_unmapped:
// pump).
func spellControllerTargetType(t *TargetFilter) game.TargetType {
	if t.Filter != "creature" {
		return ""
	}
	if *t != (TargetFilter{Filter: "creature", Controller: t.Controller}) {
		return ""
	}
	switch t.Controller {
	case "you":
		return game.TargetCreatureYouCtl
	case "opponent":
		return game.TargetCreatureOppCtl
	}
	return ""
}

func (def *CardDefinition) GetSpellEffect() *game.SpellEffect {
	// Collect any spell-type gain_energy pre-effect (e.g. Galvanic Discharge).
	gainEnergyAmount := 0
	for _, a := range def.Abilities {
		if a.Type == "spell" && a.Effect == "gain_energy" {
			if n := numToInt(a.Value["amount"]); n > 0 {
				gainEnergyAmount = n
			}
		}
	}

	eff := def.buildMainSpellEffect()
	if eff != nil && gainEnergyAmount > 0 {
		eff.GainEnergyAmount = gainEnergyAmount
	}
	return eff
}

func TestCantQuiteRecallParsing(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	oracleText := "Forbidden (This card can't be in your starting deck. Yes, you read that right. You need to figure out a way to get it into the game without it being in your deck.)\nTarget player draws three cards."

	parser := NewParser()
	result := parser.Parse(oracleText, "Instant")

	if len(result.ParseErrors) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected parse errors: %v", result.ParseErrors)
	}

	if len(result.Abilities) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 2 abilities, got %d: %+v", len(result.Abilities), result.Abilities)
	}

	var hasForbidden, hasDraw bool
	for _, ab := range result.Abilities {
		if ab.Type == "static" && ab.Effect == "forbidden" {
			hasForbidden = true
		}
		if ab.Type == "spell" && ab.Effect == "draw" {
			if ab.Target != nil && ab.Target.Filter == "player" {
				if ab.Value["amount"] == 3 {
					hasDraw = true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if !hasForbidden {
		t.Errorf("missing forbidden static ability; abilities: %+v", result.Abilities)
	}
	if !hasDraw {
		t.Errorf("missing draw spell ability targeting player for 3 cards; abilities: %+v", result.Abilities)
	}
}

// ParseCard parses a complete card definition
func (p *Parser) ParseCard(def *CardDefinition) {
	result := p.Parse(def.Text, def.Type)

	def.Abilities = append(def.Abilities, result.Abilities...)
	def.ParseErrors = result.ParseErrors
	def.Status = result.Status

	// Alternative costs are scanned independently from the main pattern
	// library — they don't replace another ability, they augment the card.
	if alt := scanAltCost(def.Text); alt != nil {
		def.Abilities = append(def.Abilities, *alt)
		// If the only "errors" were the alt-cost line, treat the card as
		// auto-parsed instead of needs-review.
		if len(def.ParseErrors) > 0 {
			cleaned := def.ParseErrors[:0]
			for _, e := range def.ParseErrors {
				if !altCostMatches(e) {
					cleaned = append(cleaned, e)
				}
			}
			def.ParseErrors = cleaned
			if len(def.ParseErrors) == 0 {
				def.Status = StatusAutoParsed
			}
		}
	}

	// Additional-cost declarations (e.g. "As an additional cost to cast this
	// spell, sacrifice a creature.") are handled inside multiline patterns but
	// need separate recognition so line-by-line fallback parsing doesn't treat
	// them as unrecognised errors.
	if cd := scanCostDeclaration(def.Text); cd != nil {
		def.Abilities = append(def.Abilities, *cd)
	// for a non-self return-to-hand cost). Same closed vocabulary as
	// TapOther (game.ActivationCost.ReturnOther / matchesReturnOtherType,
	// which reuses matchSimpleTapType), just without the untapped
	// requirement — e.g. "artifact", "land", "legendary_creature".
	ReturnOther string `json:"return_other,omitempty"`

	// ---- Paragraph Schema v2 cost extensions (Change 6, adapter step 3a) ----
	RemoveCounters *CounterCost   `json:"remove_counters,omitempty"` // Remove N TYPE counters from X
	TapOthers      *TapOthersCost `json:"tap_others,omitempty"`      // Tap N untapped X you control
	ExileCost      *ExileCost     `json:"exile,omitempty"`           // Exile self/N cards from zone
	ReturnToHand   *ReturnCost    `json:"return_to_hand,omitempty"`  // Return X to owner's hand
	Tag            string         `json:"tag,omitempty"`             // exhaust|boast|forecast|... (closed)
	RestrictionV2  string         `json:"restriction_v2,omitempty"`  // V2CostRestrictions enum
	Condition      *Condition     `json:"cost_condition,omitempty"`  // "Activate only if ..."

	// CostReductionSpec — "This ability costs {N} less to activate for each
	// X" (task-1980 static_cost_mod). Same closed dynamic count-spec shape
	// as an effect atom's value.amount_count (game/dynamic_amount.go
	// EvalDynamicAmount); passed through verbatim onto
	// game.ActivationCost.CostReductionSpec, which resolves it fresh at
	// both canPayAbilityCost and payAbilityCost time.
	CostReductionSpec map[string]interface{} `json:"cost_reduction_spec,omitempty"`
}

func TestTargetPlayerDrawsTwoCardsParsingAndConversion(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	def := &CardDefinition{
		Name: "Targeted Draw",
		Type: "Sorcery",
		Text: "Target player draws two cards.",
	}
	result := NewParser().ParseCard(def)
	if len(result.ParseErrors) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected parse errors: %v", result.ParseErrors)
	}
	if len(def.Abilities) != 1 || def.Abilities[0].Effect != "draw" {
		t.Fatalf("expected one draw spell ability, got %+v", def.Abilities)
	}
	if target := def.Abilities[0].Target; target == nil || target.Filter != "player" {
		t.Fatalf("expected chosen-player target, got %+v", def.Abilities[0].Target)
	}

	card, err := def.ToGameCard(0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ToGameCard: %v", err)
	}
	if card.SpellEffect == nil || card.SpellEffect.SpellTargetType != game.TargetPlayer {
		t.Fatalf("expected draw spell to require a player target, got %+v", card.SpellEffect)
	}
}

func TestTargetPlayerDrawsTwoCardsChosenPlayerDraws(t *testing.T) {
	gs := game.NewGame("P0", "P1", false)
	def := &CardDefinition{
		Name: "Targeted Draw",
		Type: "Sorcery",
		Text: "Target player draws two cards.",
	}
	NewParser().ParseCard(def)
	spell, err := def.ToGameCard(0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ToGameCard: %v", err)
	}
	gs.Players[0].Hand.AddCard(spell)
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		gs.Players[0].Library.AddCard(game.NewCard("P0 card", game.TypeArtifact, game.ManaCost{}, 0))
		gs.Players[1].Library.AddCard(game.NewCard("P1 card", game.TypeArtifact, game.ManaCost{}, 1))
	}

	beforeControllerHand := gs.Players[0].Hand.Count()
	beforeTargetHand := gs.Players[1].Hand.Count()
	if err := gs.CastSpellWithTargets(0, spell.ID, []game.Target{{Type: game.TargetPlayer, PlayerIdx: 1}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CastSpellWithTargets: %v", err)
	}
	if err := gs.ResolveTopOfStack(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ResolveTopOfStack: %v", err)
	}

	if got := gs.Players[1].Hand.Count() - beforeTargetHand; got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("chosen player drew %d cards, want 2", got)
	}
	if got := gs.Players[0].Hand.Count() - beforeControllerHand; got != -1 {
		t.Fatalf("controller hand changed by %d beyond the spell leaving hand, want -1", got)
	}
}

}

+package cards
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+
+	"magic-backend/game"
+)
+
+func TestTargetPlayerDrawsTwoCardsParsingAndConversion(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	def := &CardDefinition{
+		Name: "Targeted Draw",
+		Type: "Instant",
+		Text: "Target player draws two cards.",
+	}
+	NewParser().ParseCard(def)
+	if len(def.ParseErrors) != 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("unexpected parse errors: %v", def.ParseErrors)
+	}
+	if len(def.Abilities) != 1 || def.Abilities[0].Effect != "draw" {
+		t.Fatalf("expected one draw spell ability, got %+v", def.Abilities)
+	}
+	if target := def.Abilities[0].Target; target == nil || target.Filter != "player" {
+		t.Fatalf("expected chosen-player target, got %+v", def.Abilities[0].Target)
+	}
+
+	card, err := def.ToGameCard(0)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("ToGameCard: %v", err)
+	}
+	if card.SpellEffect == nil || card.SpellEffect.SpellTargetType != game.TargetPlayer {
+		t.Fatalf("expected draw spell to require a player target, got %+v", card.SpellEffect)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestTargetPlayerDrawsTwoCardsChosenPlayerDraws(t *testing.T) {
+	gs := game.NewGame("P0", "P1", false)
+	def := &CardDefinition{
+		Name: "Targeted Draw",
+		Type: "Instant",
+		Text: "Target player draws two cards.",
+	}
+	NewParser().ParseCard(def)
+	spell, err := def.ToGameCard(0)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("ToGameCard: %v", err)
+	}
+	gs.Players[0].Hand.AddCard(spell)
+	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
+		gs.Players[0].Library.AddCard(game.NewCard("P0 card", game.TypeArtifact, game.ManaCost{}, 0))
+		gs.Players[1].Library.AddCard(game.NewCard("P1 card", game.TypeArtifact, game.ManaCost{}, 1))
+	}
+
+	beforeControllerHand := gs.Players[0].Hand.Count()
+	beforeTargetHand := gs.Players[1].Hand.Count()
+	if err := gs.CastSpellWithTargets(0, spell.ID, []game.Target{{Type: game.TargetPlayer, PlayerIdx: 1}}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("CastSpellWithTargets: %v", err)
+	}
+	if err := gs.ResolveTopOfStack(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("ResolveTopOfStack: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	if got := gs.Players[1].Hand.Count() - beforeTargetHand; got != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("chosen player drew %d cards, want 2", got)
+	}
+	if got := gs.Players[0].Hand.Count() - beforeControllerHand; got != -1 {
+		t.Fatalf("controller hand changed by %d beyond the spell leaving hand, want -1", got)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestUnsupportedPlayerDrawReferencesRemainMisses(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+	for _, text := range []string{
+		"Each player draws two cards.",
+		"That player draws two cards.",
+	} {
+		def := &CardDefinition{Type: "Sorcery", Text: text}
+		NewParser().ParseCard(def)
+		if len(def.ParseErrors) == 0 {
+			t.Errorf("%q unexpectedly parsed: abilities=%+v", text, def.Abilities)
+		}
+	}
+}
